## Climate & Soil

```{r}
#| eval: false
soil_A <- read_csv(here::here("data/z6B02090 29Aug25-1126_A-E_All.csv"), skip = 3)
soil_F <- read_csv(here::here("data/z6B02089 29Aug25-1131_F-J_All.csv"), skip = 3)
colnames(soil_A) <- c("Timestamp", "Precip_C_mm", "Precip_C_rate","Shelter_E","Shelter_D","Shelter_C","Shelter_B","Shelter_A","Batt_per_A","Batt_volt_A")
colnames(soil_F) <- c("Timestamp", "Precip_H_mm", "Precip_H_rate","Shelter_J","Shelter_I","Shelter_H","Shelter_G","Shelter_F","Batt_per_F","Batt_volt_F")

soil_AJ <- full_join(soil_A, soil_F, by = join_by(Timestamp))
str(soil_AJ)
soil_AJ$Timestamp <- as_datetime(soil_AJ$Timestamp, format = "%m/%d/%y %H:%M")
soil_AJ$Shelter_E <- as.numeric(soil_AJ$Shelter_E)
soil_AJ$Shelter_D <- as.numeric(soil_AJ$Shelter_D)
soil_AJ$Shelter_J <- as.numeric(soil_AJ$Shelter_J)
  
soil_AJ_long <- soil_AJ %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = c(Shelter_A, Shelter_B, Shelter_C, Shelter_D, Shelter_E, Shelter_F, Shelter_G, Shelter_H, Shelter_I, Shelter_J),
               names_to = "Shelter")
shelter_key <- read_csv(here::here("data/Shelter Key.csv"))

soil_AJ_long_trt <- left_join(soil_AJ_long,shelter_key,by=join_by("Shelter"))

soil_AJ_long_trt$Month <- format(soil_AJ_long_trt$Timestamp,"%B")
soil_AJ_long_trt$Month_n <- as.numeric(format(soil_AJ_long_trt$Timestamp,"%m"))
soil_AJ_long_trt$Year <- as.numeric(format(soil_AJ_long_trt$Timestamp,"%Y"))

str(soil_AJ_long_trt)

  filter(Timestamp > "2022-11-01 00:00:00" & Timestamp < "2023-05-31 23:00:00")

  filter(Timestamp > "2024-11-01 00:00:00" & Timestamp < "2025-05-31 23:00:00")

str(soil_22_23)

soil_summary_22_23_m <- soil_22_23 %>% 
  group_by(Month, Month_n, Year, Treatment) %>%

  )
```

## Relative Growth Rate

### Clean up dataset

```{r}
rgr <- read_csv(here::here("data/RGR_2024.csv"))

plots <- read_csv(here::here("data/Plot_info.csv"))

rgr <- rgr %>% 
  select(
    Recorder,
    Date,
    Month,
    Plant_ID,
    Height_cm,
    Canopy_x_cm,
    Canopy_y_cm
  ) %>% 
  replace_with_na(replace = list(Height_cm = "N/A",
                                 Canopy_x_cm = "N/A",
                                 Canopy_y_cm = "N/A")) %>% 
  mutate(Height_cm = as.numeric(Height_cm),
         Canopy_x_cm = as.numeric(Canopy_x_cm),
         Canopy_y_cm = as.numeric(Canopy_y_cm))
str(rgr)
which(rgr$Canopy_x_cm == "N/A")

# Extract species code from ID
deconstruct <- function(name) {
  starts_with_23 <- substring(name,1,2) == "23"
  
  Age <- ifelse(starts_with_23,2,1)
  Sp_Code <- ifelse(starts_with_23,
                    substring(name,7,12),
                    substring(name,4,9))
  Plot <- ifelse(starts_with_23,
                 substring(name,4,5),
                 substring(name,1,2))
  out_df <- data.frame(Plant_ID = name, Age, Sp_Code,Plot, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  return(out_df)
}
out <- deconstruct(unique(rgr$Plant_ID))
unique(out$Plot)
str(out)
str(rgr)

# Extract plot, shelter letter from ID, add in block and population
rgr2 <- inner_join(rgr,out, by=join_by(Plant_ID)) 
rgr3 <- inner_join(rgr2,plots, by=join_by(Plot)) 

unique(rgr3$Sp_Code)

unique(rgr3$Shelter)

unique(rgr3$Plot)

# Find gaps, investigate

incomplete_rows <- rgr3[,c("Plant_ID","Month","Height_cm","Canopy_x_cm","Canopy_y_cm")]
incomplete_rows_2 <- incomplete_rows[!complete.cases(incomplete_rows),]
incomplete_rows_2 <- incomplete_rows_2[rowSums(is.na(incomplete_rows_2)) < 3,] # 3 for the three measurements -- if there are any rows with Height but not canopy, for example

# Investigate three odd balls

# Find and investigate outliers
# Good job for interns
# Find average and standard deviation for each species, each growth variable (make area first), per population per month
str(rgr3)
rgr3$area <- rgr3$Canopy_x_cm*rgr3$Canopy_y_cm

str(rgr3)

rgr_avgs <- rgr3 %>% 
  group_by(Sp_Code,
           Month,
           Treatment,
           Population,
           Age) %>% 
  mutate(ht_avg = mean(Height_cm, na.rm = TRUE),
            ht_sd = sd(Height_cm, na.rm = TRUE),
            area_avg = mean(area, na.rm = TRUE),
            area_sd = sd(area, na.rm = TRUE),
            x_avg = mean(Canopy_x_cm, na.rm = TRUE),
            x_sd = sd(Canopy_x_cm, na.rm = TRUE),
            y_avg = mean(Canopy_y_cm, na.rm = TRUE),
            y_sd = sd(Canopy_y_cm, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  select(Plant_ID,
         Sp_Code,
         Month,
         Age,
         Treatment,
         Population,
         Height_cm,
         ht_avg,
         ht_sd,
         area,
         area_avg,
         area_sd,
         Canopy_x_cm,
         Canopy_y_cm,
         x_avg,
         x_sd,
         y_avg,
         y_sd)

rgr_avgs <- rgr_avgs[complete.cases(rgr_avgs),]

rgr_avgs <- rgr_avgs %>% 
  mutate(ht_max = ht_avg + 3*ht_sd,
         ht_min = ht_avg - 3*ht_sd,
         area_max = area_avg + 3*area_sd,
         area_min = area_avg - 3*area_sd,
         x_max = x_avg + 3*x_sd,
         x_min = x_avg - 3*x_sd,
         y_max = y_avg + 3*y_sd,
         y_min = y_avg - 3*y_sd)

ht_outliers <-rgr_avgs[which(rgr_avgs$Height_cm > rgr_avgs$ht_max | rgr_avgs$Height_cm < rgr_avgs$ht_min),c("Plant_ID","Sp_Code","Month","Population", "Treatment", "Height_cm","ht_avg","ht_sd","ht_min","ht_max")]

area_outliers <- rgr_avgs[which(rgr_avgs$area > rgr_avgs$area_max | rgr_avgs$area < rgr_avgs$area_min),c("Plant_ID","Sp_Code","Month","Population", "Treatment", "area","area_avg","area_sd","area_min","area_max")]

x_outliers <- rgr_avgs[which(rgr_avgs$Canopy_x_cm > rgr_avgs$x_max | rgr_avgs$Canopy_x_cm < rgr_avgs$x_min),c("Plant_ID","Sp_Code","Month","Population", "Treatment", "Canopy_x_cm","x_avg","x_sd","x_min","x_max")]

y_outliers <- rgr_avgs[which(rgr_avgs$Canopy_y_cm > rgr_avgs$y_max | rgr_avgs$Canopy_y_cm < rgr_avgs$y_min),c("Plant_ID","Sp_Code","Month","Population", "Treatment", "Canopy_y_cm","y_avg","y_sd","y_min","y_max")]

## No outliers for 3 SD from mean, investigate blanks

# remove everything except plots and rgr3
rm(area_outliers
   , ht_outliers
   , incomplete_rows
   , incomplete_rows_2
   , out
   , rgr
   , rgr2
   , rgr_avgs
   , x_outliers
   , y_outliers)
```

### Create variables

```{r}
# Calculate canopy volume (height x canopy area)
head(rgr3)
rgr3$volume <- rgr3$Height_cm*rgr3$Canopy_x_cm*rgr3$Canopy_y_cm
rgr3$Date <- as.Date(rgr3$Date, tryFormats = "%m/%d/%y")
str(rgr3)

# Separate by metric

rgr_h_wide <- rgr3 %>% 
  select(Plant_ID,
         Date,
         Month,
         Height_cm) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(Height_cm)) %>%
  pivot_wider(id_cols = Plant_ID,
              names_from = Month,
              values_from = c(Date, Height_cm)) %>% 
  mutate(rgr_h_FM = (log(Height_cm_March)-log(Height_cm_February))/as.numeric((Date_March-Date_February)),
         rgr_h_MA = (log(Height_cm_April)-log(Height_cm_March))/as.numeric((Date_April-Date_March)),
         rgr_h_AM = (log(Height_cm_May)-log(Height_cm_April))/as.numeric((Date_May-Date_April)),
         rgr_h_MJ = (log(Height_cm_June)-log(Height_cm_May))/as.numeric((Date_June-Date_May)))

rgr_v_wide <- rgr3 %>% 
  select(Plant_ID,
         Date,
         Month,
         volume) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(volume)) %>%
  pivot_wider(id_cols = Plant_ID,
              names_from = Month,
              values_from = c(Date, volume)) %>% 
  mutate(rgr_v_FM = (log(volume_March)-log(volume_February))/as.numeric((Date_March-Date_February)),
         rgr_v_MA = (log(volume_April)-log(volume_March))/as.numeric((Date_April-Date_March)),
         rgr_v_AM = (log(volume_May)-log(volume_April))/as.numeric((Date_May-Date_April)),
         rgr_v_MJ = (log(volume_June)-log(volume_May))/as.numeric((Date_June-Date_May)))
  
# Join all three together but only keep rgrs, full join by Plant_ID

rgr_hv <- full_join(rgr_h_wide,rgr_v_wide,by = join_by(Plant_ID))

rgr_hv2 <- rgr_hv %>% 
  select(
    Plant_ID,
    rgr_h_FM,
    rgr_h_MA,
    rgr_h_AM,
    rgr_h_MJ,
    rgr_v_FM,
    rgr_v_MA,
    rgr_v_AM,
    rgr_v_MJ
  )

## Wooooo we did it!
## Now just need to address outliers and re-run
## For now you're done!

rm(rgr_h_wide
   , rgr_hv
   , rgr_v_wide
   , rgr3)
```

```{r}
    dplyr::select(Treatment, Precip_mm, all_of(v)) %>%

      !is.nan(.data[[v]]),

      !is.na(Precip_mm)
```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

parse_plant_id <- function(pid) {
  # Split on "."
  parts <- str_split(pid, "\\.", simplify = FALSE)
  
  map_dfr(parts, function(p) {
    # Drop any leading numeric-only segment (e.g., "23" = year prefix)
    p <- p[!str_detect(p, "^[0-9]+$")]
    # Now p[1] = plot (e.g., "A1"), p[2] = species (e.g., "SPECOD"), p[3] = individual
    tibble(
      Plot       = p[1],
      Sp_Code    = p[2],
      individual = p[3]
    )
  })
}
```

```{r}
#| eval: false
# =============================================================================
# LI-6800 QC: leaf-area correction + flagging of problematic values
#
# Input:   licor2       one row per logged observation
# Output:  licor_qc     all rows, area-corrected values (*_c) + flag columns
#          licor_clean  "exclude" rows removed, iWUE masked where unreliable
#          review_table rows needing a look, with reasons
#
# Corrected columns end in _c (A_c, E_c, Emm_c, gsw_c, gtc_c, Ci_c, Pci_c,
# CiCa_c, WUE_c). Original columns are left untouched.
# =============================================================================

# This script corrects A, E, gsw, gtc, Ci and iWUE for the actual leaf area in licor_qc.R. It then sorts each observation into “ok,” “review,” or “exclude” and lists the reason for each flag.

# How the correction works: A, E, and total conductance scale exactly by 6 / actual area, so those are rescaled directly. gsw, gtc, and Ci are then recomputed with the LI-6800 equations. The boundary-layer terms are back-calculated from each row’s own output, so the correction keeps whatever settings the machine used. Section 3 checks that the equations reproduce the machine’s logged Ci and WUE. Both differences should be near zero; if they aren’t, stop and let me know.

# Things to know before running it:
  
#   Check what area was entered on each machine. The script assumes both machines used 6 cm². If the second machine had a different area entered, the correction factor for those rows will be wrong.
# Leaves larger than 6 cm² are capped at 6, not scaled. The chamber can only hold 6 cm² of leaf, so the script treats an area over 6 as a full chamber and flags it for review.
# Leaves under 1 cm² are flagged. The correction multiplies their values more than 6×, which also magnifies measurement noise.
# iWUE will barely change after correction. A and gsw both scale with area, so the area mostly cancels out of the ratio. A and gsw themselves will change a lot.
# Thresholds are set for C3 plants. They’re grouped at the top of the script and are reasonable for Bromus. Adjust them if you have C4 species.

# The flag_summary table shows whether flags cluster on the second machine. Rows flagged “review” stay in licor_clean until you’ve looked at them in review_table.

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# ---- 1. Settings (edit these) -----------------------------------------------

# Leaf area (cm^2) the LI-6800 used in its calculations. If the second machine
# had a different area entered, make this a per-row column instead.
area_entered <- 6

thr <- list(
  area_min    = 1,     # cm^2; below this the correction (>6x) amplifies noise
  A_max       = 40,    # µmol m-2 s-1; implausibly high for most C3 leaves
  gsw_max     = 1.5,   # mol m-2 s-1; implausibly high
  gsw_min_wue = 0.02,  # mol m-2 s-1; below this A/gsw is unreliable
  wue_max     = 250,   # µmol mol-1; implausible for C3
  CiCa_min    = 0.2,   # very low Ci/Ca with positive A suggests leak/error (C3)
  CiCa_max    = 1.0,   # Ci > Ca with positive A is physically impossible
  rep_dev     = 0.30,  # relative deviation of an obs from its plant's median A
  mad_z       = 3.5    # robust z-score cutoff for species-level outliers
)

# ---- 2. Leaf-area correction ------------------------------------------------
# A, E and gtw are all divided by leaf area in the LI-6800 equations, so they
# scale exactly by (area_entered / actual_area). gsw, gtc and Ci are then
# recomputed from the corrected values. The boundary-layer terms are
# back-calculated from each row's own output, so the correction keeps whatever
# boundary-layer conductance and stomatal ratio the machine used.

licor2 <- read.csv(here::here("data/licor2.csv"))

licor_qc <- licor2 %>%
  mutate(
    WUE_source = if_else(is.na(WUE), "manual (2nd machine)", "machine"),
    
    leaf_area = case_when(
      is.na(total.leaf.area) | total.leaf.area <= 0 ~ NA_real_,
      total.leaf.area > area_entered ~ area_entered,  # leaf larger than aperture
      TRUE ~ total.leaf.area
    ),
    area_factor = area_entered / leaf_area,
    
    # Back-calculated terms from the machine's own output
    r_bw  = 1 / gtw - 1 / gsw,        # boundary-layer term, water
    r_bc  = 1 / gtc - 1.6 / gsw,      # boundary-layer term, CO2
    P_kPa = 1000 * Pca / Ca,          # chamber pressure
    
    # Fluxes scale directly with 1/area
    A_c   = A   * area_factor,
    E_c   = E   * area_factor,
    Emm_c = E_c * 1000,
    gtw_c = gtw * area_factor,
    
    # Recompute conductances and Ci
    gsw_den = 1 / gtw_c - r_bw,
    gsw_c   = if_else(gsw_den > 0, 1 / gsw_den, NA_real_),
    gtc_c   = 1 / (1.6 / gsw_c + r_bc),
    Ci_c    = ((gtc_c - E_c / 2) * Ca - A_c) / (gtc_c + E_c / 2),
    Pci_c   = Ci_c * P_kPa / 1000,
    CiCa_c  = Ci_c / Ca,
    
    # Intrinsic WUE (A/gsw) for every row, including the missing ones
    WUE_c   = A_c / gsw_c
  )

# ---- 3. Sanity checks: do the equations reproduce the machine's output? -----
# Both differences should be tiny (rounding only). If not, stop and check.

ci_diff  <- with(licor_qc, ((gtc - E / 2) * Ca - A) / (gtc + E / 2) - Ci)
wue_diff <- with(licor_qc, A / gsw - WUE)
cat("Max |Ci reconstructed - Ci logged|: ",
    round(max(abs(ci_diff), na.rm = TRUE), 3), "ppm\n")
cat("Max |A/gsw - WUE logged|:           ",
    round(max(abs(wue_diff), na.rm = TRUE), 3), "\n")

# ---- 4. Replicate stability and species-level outliers ----------------------

safe_z <- function(x) {
  m <- mad(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (is.na(m) || m == 0) return(rep(NA_real_, length(x)))
  (x - median(x, na.rm = TRUE)) / m
}

licor_qc <- licor_qc %>%
  group_by(Plant_ID, Date) %>%
  mutate(
    n_obs   = n(),
    A_med   = median(A_c, na.rm = TRUE),
    rep_dev = abs(A_c - A_med) / pmax(abs(A_med), 1)  # floor avoids blow-up near 0
  ) %>%
  group_by(Sp_Code) %>%
  mutate(
    z_A   = safe_z(A_c),
    z_WUE = safe_z(WUE_c)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# ---- 5. Flags ---------------------------------------------------------------
# h_ = hard flags: technical failure or physically impossible -> exclude
# s_ = soft flags: unusual but possibly real biology          -> review

licor_qc <- licor_qc %>%
  mutate(
    # Hard
    h_area_missing      = is.na(leaf_area),
    h_correction_failed = !is.na(leaf_area) & is.na(gsw_c),
    h_Ci_negative       = !is.na(Ci_c) & Ci_c < 0,
    h_Ci_gt_Ca          = !is.na(CiCa_c) & CiCa_c > thr$CiCa_max & A_c > 0,
    
    # Soft
    s_area_capped  = !is.na(total.leaf.area) & total.leaf.area > area_entered,
    s_area_small   = !is.na(leaf_area) & leaf_area < thr$area_min,
    s_A_negative   = !is.na(A_c) & A_c < 0,
    s_A_high       = !is.na(A_c) & A_c > thr$A_max,
    s_E_negative   = !is.na(E_c) & E_c < 0,
    s_gsw_low      = !is.na(gsw_c) & gsw_c < thr$gsw_min_wue,
    s_gsw_high     = !is.na(gsw_c) & gsw_c > thr$gsw_max,
    s_WUE_high     = !is.na(WUE_c) & WUE_c > thr$wue_max,
    s_CiCa_low     = !is.na(CiCa_c) & CiCa_c < thr$CiCa_min & A_c > 0,
    s_unstable_rep = n_obs > 1 & !is.na(rep_dev) & rep_dev > thr$rep_dev,
    s_outlier_A    = !is.na(z_A)   & abs(z_A)   > thr$mad_z,
    s_outlier_WUE  = !is.na(z_WUE) & abs(z_WUE) > thr$mad_z
  )

hard_flags <- grep("^h_", names(licor_qc), value = TRUE)
soft_flags <- grep("^s_", names(licor_qc), value = TRUE)

list_flags <- function(df, cols) {
  m <- as.matrix(df[cols])
  apply(m, 1, function(r) paste(cols[r], collapse = "; "))
}

licor_qc$hard_reasons <- list_flags(licor_qc, hard_flags)
licor_qc$soft_reasons <- list_flags(licor_qc, soft_flags)

licor_qc <- licor_qc %>%
  mutate(qc_status = case_when(
    hard_reasons != "" ~ "exclude",
    soft_reasons != "" ~ "review",
    TRUE               ~ "ok"
  ))

# ---- 6. Summaries -----------------------------------------------------------

# How many rows are ok / review / exclude, by data source
licor_qc %>% count(WUE_source, qc_status) %>% print()

# Which flags fire, and whether they cluster on one machine
flag_summary <- licor_qc %>%
  group_by(WUE_source) %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(c(hard_flags, soft_flags)), sum), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_longer(-WUE_source, names_to = "flag", values_to = "n") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = WUE_source, values_from = n) %>%
  arrange(flag)
print(flag_summary, n = Inf)

# Rows to inspect by hand
review_table <- licor_qc %>%
  filter(qc_status != "ok") %>%
  select(Plant_ID, Sp_Code, Plot, Date, obs, WUE_source, qc_status,
         total.leaf.area, A, A_c, gsw_c, Ci_c, CiCa_c, WUE_c,
         hard_reasons, soft_reasons) %>%
  arrange(desc(qc_status), Plant_ID, obs)
print(review_table, n = 50)
write.csv(review_table, here::here("data/licor_review_table.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# ---- 7. Clean dataset -------------------------------------------------------
# Drops hard-flagged rows and masks iWUE where gsw is too low for the ratio
# to be meaningful (A and gsw themselves are kept). Soft-flagged rows stay in;
# decide on those after reviewing, and run analyses with and without them.

licor_clean <- licor_qc %>%
  filter(qc_status != "exclude") %>%
  mutate(WUE_clean = if_else(gsw_c < thr$gsw_min_wue, NA_real_, WUE_c))

write.csv(licor_clean,here::here("data/licor_clean.csv"))

# ---- 8. Quick visual check --------------------------------------------------

ggplot(licor_qc, aes(gsw_c, A_c, colour = qc_status, shape = WUE_source)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(ok = "grey50", review = "orange",
                                 exclude = "red")) +
  labs(x = expression(g[sw]~"(mol m"^-2~"s"^-1*", area-corrected)"),
       y = expression(A~"(µmol m"^-2~"s"^-1*", area-corrected)"),
       colour = "QC status", shape = "Source") +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r}
cn <- read_csv(here::here("data/cn.csv"))
str(cn)
cn$Plant_ID <- cn$`Sample ID`

library(dplyr)
library(stringr)

#' Deconstruct plant IDs into their component parts
#'
#' Handles all of these forms (and combinations of them):
#'   A1.STIPUL.1        basic: plot A1, species STIPUL, individual 1
#'   23.A1.STIPUL.1     cohort prefix (1 yr old at collection)
#'   A1.STIPUL.1-G6     substitute individual taken from plot G6
#'   A1.STIPUL.1-2      second sample from the same individual
#'   A1.STIPUL.1a / 1b  two subsamples of the same leaf
#'   23.A1.STIPUL.1-G6-2  any combination of the above
#'
#' @param df     data frame containing the ID column
#' @param id_col name of the ID column (default "Sample ID")
#' @return df with parsed columns inserted right after the ID column,
#'         all original columns retained
parse_plant_id <- function(df, id_col = "Sample ID") {

  # find the ID column, tolerating odd spacing/case in the header
  # (e.g. "Sample ID " or a non-breaking space from Excel)
  norm <- function(x) tolower(gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]", "", x))
  hit  <- names(df)[norm(names(df)) == norm(id_col)]
  if (length(hit) != 1) {
    stop("Couldn't find a column called '", id_col, "'. Columns are:\n  ",
         paste(names(df), collapse = "\n  "),
         "\nPass the right one with id_col = \"...\"", call. = FALSE)
  }
  id_col <- hit
  ids <- str_trim(as.character(df[[id_col]]))

  # 1 cohort | 2 structure | 3 plot no. | 4 genus | 5 epithet | 6 individual | 7 suffixes
  pattern <- paste0(
    "^(?:(\\d{2})\\.)?",              # optional 2-digit cohort prefix, e.g. "23."
    "([A-Za-z]+)(\\d+)\\.",           # plot: structure letter(s) + plot number
    "([A-Za-z]{3})([A-Za-z]{3})\\.",  # 6-letter species code (genus + epithet)
    "(\\d+)",                         # individual number
    "([A-Za-z]?)",                    # optional a/b = subsample of the same leaf
    "((?:-[A-Za-z0-9]+)*)$"           # zero or more "-xx" suffixes
  )
  m <- str_match(ids, pattern)

  suffix <- m[, 9]
  # "-G6" style suffix (letters + digits) = plot the substitute came from
  donor  <- str_match(suffix, "-([A-Za-z]+\\d+)(?=-|$)")[, 2]
  # "-2" style suffix (digits only) = repeat sample from same individual
  rep    <- str_match(suffix, "-(\\d+)(?=-|$)")[, 2]

  parsed <- tibble(
    parse_ok       = !is.na(m[, 1]),
    cohort         = m[, 2],
    one_year_old   = !is.na(m[, 2]),
    structure      = toupper(m[, 3]),
    plot_num       = as.integer(m[, 4]),
    Plot           = paste0(toupper(m[, 3]), m[, 4]),
    Sp_Code   = toupper(paste0(m[, 5], m[, 6])),
    genus_code     = toupper(m[, 5]),
    epithet_code   = toupper(m[, 6]),
    individual     = as.integer(m[, 7]),
    leaf_subsample = na_if(tolower(m[, 8]), ""),  # "a"/"b", NA if none
    is_subsample   = !is.na(leaf_subsample),
    substitute     = !is.na(donor),
    source_plot    = toupper(donor),     # NA unless "-G6" style suffix
    sample_rep     = as.integer(coalesce(rep, "1")),
    is_resample    = !is.na(rep)
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      # clean up rows that didn't parse (standards, blanks, typos)
      across(-parse_ok, ~ if_else(parse_ok, .x, NA)),
      Plot = if_else(parse_ok, Plot, NA_character_),
      # plot the tissue physically came from
      collected_from = coalesce(source_plot, Plot),
      # one key per physical plant (drops a/b and the "-2" replicate),
      # handy for averaging all samples from a plant
      plant_key = if_else(
        parse_ok,
        paste0(
          if_else(is.na(cohort), "", paste0(cohort, ".")),
          Plot, ".", Sp_Code, ".", individual,
          if_else(is.na(source_plot), "", paste0("-", source_plot))
        ),
        NA_character_
      ),
      # one key per leaf sample: keeps the "-2" replicate, drops a/b,
      # so a/b subsamples of the same leaf share a key
      leaf_key = if_else(parse_ok, paste0(plant_key, "_rep", sample_rep),
                         NA_character_)
    )

  if (any(!parsed$parse_ok)) {
    bad <- unique(ids[!parsed$parse_ok])
    warning(length(bad), " ID(s) did not match any known format: ",
            paste(head(bad, 10), collapse = ", "),
            if (length(bad) > 10) ", ..." else "", call. = FALSE)
  }

  # keep every original column, parsed columns sit right after the ID
  bind_cols(df, parsed) %>%
    relocate(all_of(names(parsed)), .after = all_of(id_col))
}

# ---- usage ----
# cn_parsed <- parse_plant_id(cn)                       # uses "Sample ID"
# cn_parsed <- parse_plant_id(cn, id_col = "Plant_ID")  # if you renamed it
#
# filter(cn_parsed, !parse_ok)   # inspect anything that didn't parse
#
# # average a/b subsamples to one row per leaf sample:
# cn_parsed %>%
#   group_by(leaf_key, plant_key, plot, species_code, cohort) %>%
#   summarise(across(c(`%N`, `δ13CVPDB (‰)`, `δ15NAir (‰)`), mean), .groups = "drop")
#
# # average all samples to one row per plant:
```

```{r}

lf_area <- read_csv(here::here("data/LMA_lf_area.csv"))
str(lf_area)

# =====================================================================

#' Deconstruct leaf-area sample IDs
#'
#' Same pieces as parse_plant_id(), for IDs written without dots, e.g.
#'   C8AIRCAR2_20240505        plot C8, AIRCAR, individual 2, collected 2024-05-05
#'   A1AIRCAR2_I6_20240505     ... substitute individual taken from plot I6
#' Also accepts a cohort prefix ("23A1..." or "23.A1..."), a/b leaf
#' subsamples ("...2a_..."), a short repeat number ("_2"), and "." / "_" / "-"
#' separators. Anything written after the date is kept as a note:
#'   A6BROHOR1_20240503ligule, E4AVEBAR1_20240505 two pieces,
#'   A6AVEFAT1_20240503_too small
#' Any other suffix piece it doesn't recognise makes parse_ok FALSE.
#'
#' Output keys (plant_key, leaf_key) are built exactly as in
#' parse_plant_id(), so the two tables can be joined.
#'
#' @param df     data frame containing the ID column
#' @param id_col name of the ID column (default "sample")
parse_leaf_area_id <- function(df, id_col = "sample") {

  norm <- function(x) tolower(gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]", "", x))
  hit  <- names(df)[norm(names(df)) == norm(id_col)]
  if (length(hit) != 1) {
    stop("Couldn't find a column called '", id_col, "'. Columns are:\n  ",
         paste(names(df), collapse = "\n  "),
         "\nPass the right one with id_col = \"...\"", call. = FALSE)
  }
  id_col <- hit
  ids <- str_trim(as.character(df[[id_col]]))

  # Step 1: split off the 8-digit date and anything written after it.
  #   "A6BROHOR1_20240503ligule"      -> core "A6BROHOR1", note "ligule"
  #   "E4AVEBAR1_20240505 two pieces" -> core "E4AVEBAR1", note "two pieces"
  #   "A6AVEFAT1_20240503_too small"  -> core "A6AVEFAT1", note "too small"
  d <- str_match(ids, "^(.*?)[_ -]*(\\d{8})(.*)$")
  has_date <- !is.na(d[, 1])
  core     <- if_else(has_date, d[, 2], ids)
  date_raw <- d[, 3]
  notes    <- na_if(str_trim(str_remove(d[, 4], "^[_ .-]+")), "")

  # Step 2: parse the plant ID part.
  # 1 cohort | 2 structure | 3 plot no. | 4 genus | 5 epithet |
  # 6 individual | 7 a/b | 8 suffixes
  pattern <- paste0(
    "^(?:(\\d{2})[._-]?)?",            # optional cohort prefix, e.g. "23"
    "([A-Za-z]+)(\\d+)[._-]?",         # plot, e.g. "A1"
    "([A-Za-z]{3})([A-Za-z]{3})[._-]?",# 6-letter species code
    "(\\d+)([A-Za-z]?)",               # individual + optional a/b
    "((?:[_-][A-Za-z0-9]+)*)$"         # "_I6", "_2", ...
  )
  m <- str_match(core, pattern)

  # sort each suffix piece by what it looks like
  tokens <- str_split(str_remove(m[, 9], "^[_-]"), "[_-]")
  is_donor <- function(t) str_detect(t, "^[A-Za-z]+\\d+$")   # "I6"
  is_rep   <- function(t) str_detect(t, "^\\d{1,2}$")        # "2"
  pick <- function(f) vapply(tokens, function(t) {
    t <- t[which(f(t))]; if (length(t)) t[1] else NA_character_
  }, character(1))
  suffix_ok <- vapply(tokens, function(t) {
    t <- t[t != "" & !is.na(t)]
    all(is_donor(t) | is_rep(t))
  }, logical(1))

  donor    <- pick(is_donor)
  rep      <- pick(is_rep)

  parsed <- tibble(
    parse_ok        = !is.na(m[, 1]) & suffix_ok,
    cohort          = m[, 2],
    one_year_old    = !is.na(m[, 2]),
    structure       = toupper(m[, 3]),
    plot_num        = as.integer(m[, 4]),
    Plot            = paste0(toupper(m[, 3]), m[, 4]),
    Sp_Code         = toupper(paste0(m[, 5], m[, 6])),
    genus_code      = toupper(m[, 5]),
    epithet_code    = toupper(m[, 6]),
    individual      = as.integer(m[, 7]),
    leaf_subsample  = na_if(tolower(m[, 8]), ""),
    is_subsample    = !is.na(leaf_subsample),
    substitute      = !is.na(donor),
    source_plot     = toupper(donor),
    sample_rep      = as.integer(coalesce(rep, "1")),
    is_resample     = !is.na(rep),
    collection_date = as.Date(date_raw, format = "%Y%m%d"),
    notes           = notes,              # free text after the date
    has_note        = !is.na(notes)
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      # blank out parsed fields for bad IDs, but keep date and notes
      across(-c(parse_ok, collection_date, notes, has_note),
             ~ if_else(parse_ok, .x, NA)),
      collected_from = coalesce(source_plot, Plot),
      plant_key = if_else(
        parse_ok,
        paste0(
          if_else(is.na(cohort), "", paste0(cohort, ".")),
          Plot, ".", Sp_Code, ".", individual,
          if_else(is.na(source_plot), "", paste0("-", source_plot))
        ),
        NA_character_
      ),
      leaf_key = if_else(parse_ok, paste0(plant_key, "_rep", sample_rep),
                         NA_character_)
    )

  if (any(!parsed$parse_ok)) {
    bad <- unique(ids[!parsed$parse_ok])
    warning(length(bad), " ID(s) did not match any known format: ",
            paste(head(bad, 10), collapse = ", "),
            if (length(bad) > 10) ", ..." else "",
            "\nSee them all with filter(<result>, !parse_ok)", call. = FALSE)
  }

  bind_cols(df, parsed) %>%
    relocate(all_of(names(parsed)), .after = all_of(id_col))
}
```
